piezas.titular: INTEF updates its guide to AI in education with ten ethical principles and a phased plan for schools to adopt it
piezas.entradilla: Version 2.0 of the Ministry of Education's guide, published in September 2026, organises the use of AI around three profiles (students, teachers and schools) and adds annexes ready for the classroom.
cuerpo: The [Guide on the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Education](https://intef.es/Noticias/nueva-version-de-la-guia-sobre-el-uso-de-la-inteligencia-artificial-en-el-ambito-educativo/) is published by the National Institute of Educational Technologies and Teacher Training (INTEF), part of the Ministry of Education, Vocational Training and Sport. Version 2.0 dates from September 2026 and updates the first edition, from 2024. It is aimed at three profiles: students, teachers and schools. It is in Spanish, runs to more than a hundred pages and is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0. It remains useful as the reference document of the state education administration.

Its starting point is that “The central question should not be, therefore, whether or not AI is used, but how, for what purpose and under what conditions”. It places AI literacy in four domains (engaging, creating, managing and designing), taken from the framework that the OECD and the European Commission published in 2026, [which was also shared in the library](https://t.me/ChatGPTedu/21753/49714) under the title “How to Prepare Students for the Age of AI”. For each profile it includes a table of challenges with preventive measures. For students, these include cognitive offloading and the “illusion of competence”; the measures include tasks that make the process visible, oral defences and practice without AI in the early stages of learning.

For teachers, the guide points out that the European AI Act classifies systems intended to assess learning outcomes as high-risk: it does not forbid assessing with AI, but it imposes obligations on whoever deploys it. It distinguishes between grading and offering continuous feedback, and mentions draft feedback that the teacher supervises. Where students have autonomy, it proposes guided self-assessment with rubrics designed by the teacher. On data protection, it recalls that Spanish law only allows processing to be based on a person's own consent from the age of 14.

For schools, it proposes integrating AI into the school's Digital Plan rather than treating it as a sum of isolated initiatives by individual teachers, in seven phases: a coordinating committee, analysis of the starting situation, review of the regulations, objectives, lines of action, gradual implementation, and monitoring and review. It recommends prioritising tools provided or authorised by the education authorities, informing families, and watching for the emergence of dependencies and for the impact on equity and digital wellbeing. The regulation it cites is [Regulation (EU) 2024/1689](https://t.me/ChatGPTedu/21753/34057), also present in the library.

Among the new features is the ethics section, with ten principles (a person-centred approach, academic integrity, equality of opportunity, human oversight, educational purpose, transparency, privacy, responsible use, wellbeing and sustainability, and reflection and anticipation). Each comes with a good practice and a practice to review; for example, assessing a task without knowing which part was generated by AI. Another new feature is the environmental section, which gathers data from other sources: according to the guide, a query to a generative AI uses ten times more electricity than a traditional search, and between ten and fifty questions are equivalent to half a litre of water. These figures come from studies listed in its references; the guide does not verify them itself.

The limits are those of an institutional guide: it provides no data of its own on classroom results, its legal framework is Spanish and European, and many of its recommendations are general. The document states that some illustrations were produced with ChatGPT and that ChatGPT and Gemini were used for language support, with final approval of the contents resting with INTEF. The library also has [version 3.0 of INTEF's Guidelines on digital tools and data protection](https://t.me/ChatGPTedu/21753/50331), from the same body and focused on a subject that this guide covers only in part.

For a teacher, the most useful material comes at the end. Annex 1 proposes learning situations by stage, key competence and AI literacy domain. Annex 2 is a model statement of AI use for students, and Annex 3 is a ten-question reflection questionnaire to find out their starting point. To begin, it is worth reading the table of challenges for the relevant profile, then moving on to the ten principles and, for a school leadership team, to the seven phases in section 2.3.2.

piezas.comprobado: Revisor: contrastado con el texto completo del PDF de la entrada (cita literal, desafíos y medidas de la tabla 1, Reglamento y alto riesgo, edad de 14 años, siete fases de 2.3.2, diez principios con buena práctica y práctica a revisar, cifras ambientales, anexos 1 a 3, nota final sobre ChatGPT y Gemini, primera versión de 2024). La noticia oficial del INTEF (intef.es, 8 de septiembre de 2026) confirma versión 2.0, septiembre de 2026, novedades y licencia CC BY-SA; su enlace de descarga (run.gob.es) lleva a un PDF del INTEF cuyo número de páginas no se pudo contrastar con el de la entrada, por eso el enlace del documento es la noticia oficial. Las cifras ambientales y la edad de 14 años son las que da la guía, sin comprobar en sus fuentes. Los títulos de los tres documentos de la biblioteca enlazados figuran en la lista de la entrada (el de la OCDE/Comisión Europea es la referencia que cita la guía); no se abrieron esos documentos. No hay piezas publicadas sobre esta guía en publicado.txt. Vigencia: sin edición posterior encontrada.
piezas.ilustracion: Esquema en tres columnas (alumnado, profesorado, centro) sobre una base común con los cuatro ámbitos de la alfabetización en IA (interactuar, crear, gestionar, modelar); sobre la columna del centro, una escalera de siete peldaños que acaba en un círculo de revisión.
piezas.ilustracion_alt: Three cards, each with a human figure, labelled “Students”, “Teachers” and “School”, resting on a base labelled “Four domains”; above the school card a seven-step staircase labelled “Seven phases” rises to a circle with a review arrow.
repaso: Quitado «adopta como marco el Reglamento europeo de IA» (el texto lo trata como contexto normativo, no como marco adoptado).
Quitado «etapas no universitarias» (no confirmado en el texto) y «unas 114 páginas», sustituido por «más de cien páginas».
«Delegación ciega» no es un desafío de la tabla: se quita de la lista de desafíos del alumnado; añadida la medida de práctica sin IA en fases iniciales, que sí figura en la tabla.
Orientaciones v3.0: se quita que «se ocupa en detalle» del tema de datos (solo consta su título en la entrada); se deja la relación comprobable.
Precisado que el priorizar herramientas es de las puestas a disposición o autorizadas por las administraciones educativas, y que las cifras ambientales son «según la guía».
Recortado el cuerpo a menos de 700 palabras (quitado «aprender para, con y sobre la IA», que no se pudo confirmar, y duplicidades).
